depth.needCards: Flat OutlinedCard with no custom shadow or hover lift.

motion.policy: Current Material controls, interaction feedback, and progress indicators; no custom duration token or transition choreography is established.

componentSources.name: Native actions and fields
componentSources.description: Material controls, written labels, keyboard-specific inputs, password masking, and busy/disabled actions.

componentSources.name: Native navigation
componentSources.description: Needs, Field, Nearby, Saved; Team action in app bar. Shared contextual Back closes form, then detail, then returns to Needs.

componentSources.name: Need filters
componentSources.description: Active/Completed state and category selection share one horizontally scrolling row.

componentSources.name: NeedCard
componentSources.description: Title, quantity, organization, and complete action precede supporting metadata. Completed uses received quantities/progress, View impact, Help has arrived, and no urgency.

componentSources.name: Notice and freshness
componentSources.description: Explicit snapshot time, current connection capability, nonproduction disclosure, and dismissible general feedback.

componentSources.name: Request detail eligibility
componentSources.description: New contribution controls require verified organization, eligible nonterminal status, valid future deadline, and positive remaining quantity. Unavailable states show recovery guidance.

componentSources.name: Nearby decisions
componentSources.description: Matching-code pairing, file receipt, incoming calls, and permission actions; nearby connection does not verify identity.

componentSources.name: Saved work and delivery stages
componentSources.description: Separate drafts, signed updates, pending operations, contributions, files, messages, and original-action retries; error text for rejection/conflict/invalidation.

componentSources.name: Same-account recovery
componentSources.description: Sign-in recovery preserves saved work and signing identity, with explicit same-account guidance.

android.previewPolicy: Top-level HTML/CSS specimens remain the established web components. Native components are documented from Compose sources and device/emulator captures, not HTML facsimiles.

assets.capturePolicy: Review PNGs are ignored local-only QA evidence, not shipping artwork or public Git artifacts.

narrative.thesis: A readable community noticeboard that keeps relief quantities and saved-work status understandable in the field.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Pair every status color with written state. Nearby connection is not volunteer verification, and local saving is not publication.

rules.name: The Heading First Rule
rules.body: Keep the human-readable need title ahead of quantity, category, and organization metadata.

rules.name: The Task First Rule
rules.body: Preserve the reviewed normal-phone path from compact invitation to search, filters, freshness, and the first need's quantity, organization, and complete action. Large text, landscape, and keyboard states may continue below the viewport through scrolling; the captures do not prove all device/font combinations.

review.visibility: Verdict and captures are ignored local-only QA evidence; these paths are not public Git links.
review.scope: Exactly the original four material findings; all four resolved. Fix-list verdict only, not whole-surface, independent gesture/device, transport, or production certification.
sourceOnlyEvidence: Common contextual callback assignment for system and visible app-bar Back
review.detector: Skipped: native Kotlin/Compose is not HTML/CSS.

narrative.overview:
Saathi is a calm, humane place to find a verified need, check its current quantities, and coordinate help. Warm paper surfaces, forest ink, short Lora headings, and precise Manrope controls make the interface approachable while keeping operational information legible. The noticeboard is the recorded direction: approachable need cards, chronological field reports, and durable request notices.

The built world is text-led and task-first. Thin rules separate evidence, actions, and field updates; icons clarify labels rather than replace them. There is no decorative hero imagery. User-supplied photos and videos belong inside field reports. Light and dark themes preserve the same semantic hierarchy. The product commitments remain calm, credible, accessible, politically neutral, and free of flashy startup presentation or gamification.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and forest ink with restrained teal actions.
Humane serif page headings with compact, legible sans-serif data.
Flat, bordered surfaces and explicit quantities, deadlines, and verification.
Mobile task clarity with persistent public navigation.
Current status and permanent closed notices over stale shared screenshots.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Use color with visible status text or a recognizable control. Urgency, verification, fulfillment, and failure must remain understandable without color.

rules.name: The Heading First Rule
rules.body: Lead a card or detail header with the human-readable title. Category, priority, request ID, and organization metadata follow it.

rules.name: The Task First Rule
rules.body: On the needs surface, keep the route to a usable request short: compact explanation, heading, search, filters, then need cards. Supporting trust copy must not push the first request action below mobile navigation.

rules.name: The Flat Noticeboard Rule
rules.body: Use tonal surfaces and thin rules to group information. Do not add decorative shadows or hover lifts to the existing noticeboard.

dos: **Do** preserve the community noticeboard: warm paper, humane short headings, flat surfaces, and thin rules.
**Do** put human-readable headings before category, ID, and organization metadata.
**Do** keep remaining quantity, verification, and the next action clear on a narrow screen.
**Do** pair status color with explicit text and maintain the same semantics in both themes.
**Do** keep permanent request notices readable when a shared link outlives a need.
**Do** use visible keyboard focus, written control labels, and the existing reduced-motion behavior.
**Do** show genuine field media in its report context and label demonstration content.
donts: **Don't** add flashy startup presentation, gamification, decorative shadows, or hover lifts.
**Don't** replace operational quantity bars with decorative progress or invented impact statistics.
**Don't** imply verification when the organization’s verification is unavailable.
**Don't** leave a donation form in a closed, unavailable-verification, or fully committed request state.
**Don't** let supporting trust copy hide the first usable need below fixed mobile navigation.
**Don't** invent real relief operations, partners, testimonials, or imagery from the demonstration records.
